claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy is single phase.
The single phase in equimolar WTaTiVZr is likely BCC.
The multi-principal-element composition produces high chemical disorder and local chemical fluctuations in WTaTiVZr.
Chemical disorder in WTaTiVZr induces significant atomic-scale local lattice distortions.
Localized lattice strain fields lower the critical resolved shear stress for dislocation slip.
The lattice distortions permit multiple dislocation slip systems to operate simultaneously.
Interactions between multiple principal elements and dislocations affect dislocation motion.
Improved lattice diffusion in WTaTiVZr promotes diffusion-assisted dislocation motion and dynamic recovery.
Activation of multiple slip systems and enhanced dynamic recovery delay dislocation pile-up.
Delayed dislocation pile-up postpones premature crack initiation and crack propagation.
The proposed dislocation processes cause greater plasticity and improved toughness.
Under matched high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher plastic strain at failure than pure tungsten.
Under matched high-temperature creep loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit a lower creep rate than pure tungsten.
Under matched high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten is relevant to plasma-facing-component service but is limited by a high ductile-to-brittle transition temperature and embrittlement.
The proposed mechanism applies under high-temperature conditions relevant to plasma-facing components when grain sizes and microstructural homogeneity are comparable.

contradictions.description: The mechanism invokes lower slip resistance, improved lattice diffusion, and diffusion-assisted dislocation motion, all of which can facilitate high-temperature deformation, yet it predicts a lower creep rate without identifying a countervailing creep-strengthening process.
